title: Negative: with cooperative catalysis and weak enzyme turnover on a consumed fuel, condensates nucleated from noise grow and stretch into rods but never divide (0 splits on 2 seeds, 256^2, t=12000); on a fuel reservoir the same world gives a static field of small round droplets
summary: world.py: c23's CIPS-fuel world with catalysis kc F e^2 (1-p) (kc=2), De=0.1, chi=3, DF=2, kF=0.2, and uniform fuel-independent enzyme turnover d(e0-e), d=0.0003, e0=0.12, from uniform e0 plus noise 0.02. labkit packs on seeds 0 and 1 (pack/s0, pack/s1): after a long quiet period, bodies nucleate one by one from t~4000. Each grows (persistent-track area ratio 27 and 18), most stretch into rods 3-5 diameters long, and one per run hollows into a ring that opens into a hook (pack/s0/sheet.png t=5750-8850). At t=12000 there are 18 and 16 bodies, every one of them nucleated (18 and 16 nucleations): 0 splits, 0 merges, 0 movement. In the reservoir twin (F held at 1, hold_twin_screen.png, seed 0, t=10000) 35 small round droplets nucleate by t~1000 and stay static. A planted founder on 256^2 grows into a ring that only widens for 10000 t (founder_ring_256.png). So the consumed fuel delays nucleation, gives fewer and larger bodies, and lets them elongate, but no route to division appeared. The rods all lie along the grid diagonals, so their orientation, and perhaps the elongation itself, may be grid anisotropy of the dimension-split drift; my Lsc=5 test in 20261026T0218 rounded a ring but was not run on rods. The fission seen in 20261026T0233-c35-cips-coop-fission-sighting needed a planted ellipse and happened once per body.

finding.operator: cooperative (second-order) catalysis plus uniform enzyme turnover in catalysis-induced phase separation on a consumed, regrowing fuel
finding.result: consumed fuel: 18/16 bodies at t=12000, all nucleated, 0 splits, 0 merges, area ratio 27/18 (rods); reservoir: 35 small round static droplets
